transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-05-18 13:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Renee (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Brightline Platform), Priya (Brightline DS), Evan (Brightline Infra), Sara (Brightline Security), Tom (Brightline PM)

Topics (auto): staging connectivity, KV cache bench, SSO/KMS, ops handoff, next steps

[00:00] Maya Gonzalez: hi everyone thanks for joining on time, quick roll call?
[00:05] Jordan Lee: hey Jordan here, platform eng, all good
[00:07] Priya Sharma: Priya, data science, running the evals
[00:09] Evan Mills: Evan infra - brought the routing questions
[00:11] Sara Kim: Sara security - SOC2 checklist questions ready
[00:14] Maya Gonzalez: great, Liam do you want to walk through the bench results you ran overnight?
[00:19] Liam O'Connor: yeah quick summary. ran three profiles: small chat (128 tokens), typical UI request (512) and large batch (2k). curious things: with KV cache on we saw p50 drop from 210ms to 95ms for 512 tokens, p95 from 820ms to 360ms, but the tail beyond 990th was spiky due to a serialization backlog on one node.
[00:45] Priya Sharma: can you repeat the node spike bit, was that GPU memory thrash or network?
[00:48] Liam O'Connor: it looked like network retransmits in the logs, there were a handful of requests that hit a node packing multiple quantized shards and its event loop got backlogged, so small queuing. we suspect an orchestration placement bug when autoscaler relocated a replica mid-run.
[01:15] Evan Mills: that matches what we saw - when we repro'd in staging the kube node started oxy something (inaudible) and pods were evicted briefly. i can share the kube events.
[01:28] Jordan Lee: we also saw weird tokenization differences on our end - sometimes longer prompts got truncated earlier than expected, might be client SDK mismatch version.
[01:35] Priya Sharma: yes that affected the eval scoring - truncation made some summaries worse so we gated the quality numbers.
[01:40] Liam O'Connor: SDK mismatch makes sense; we shipped a small patch last week that changes prompt pre-encoding. i'll post the exact version string we ran against.
[02:05] Maya Gonzalez: on the security front Sara had some questions about KMS and audit logs, do you want to go through them now?
[02:10] Sara Kim: sure. primary ask is: can we bring our customer-managed KMS key for encrypting model cache and any persisted payloads? also need audit logs for inference requests at token granularity or at least per-request with payload hash. how durable are logs and retention policy?
[02:33] Liam O'Connor: for private deployments yes you can bring your KMS. for hosted pilot we can integrate with your KMS via envelope keys, but that requires a brief onboarding step and HSM-level permissions; i'll share docs. audit logs: we emit per-request metadata, timestamps, model id, route and hashes; we can increase retention for pilot but long-term retention is configurable via enterprise add-on.
[02:58] Sara Kim: okay we'll need a scope doc for SOC2 box checks - can you map which controls are covered by Redwood hosted vs what Brightline must provide?
[03:07] Maya Gonzalez: yes we'll create a scoping matrix. i'll include compliance PM and our security contact.
[03:14] Tom Alvarez: quick question on SSO - we tried SAML test yesterday but the provider timed out. is Redwood on the SAML IdP standard flow or do you do any special certs?
[03:21] Liam O'Connor: standard SAML 2.0. certs are standard x509. timeout could be due to ACS URL mismatch or a clock skews - if you send the SAML response logs we can triage.
[03:37] Evan Mills: about staging networking - we posted a peering request but the route tables didn't propagate, how should we verify?
[03:42] Maya Gonzalez: Jordan you and Evan should send the route table screenshots to Renee and Liam. we'll verify on our side.
[03:49] Jordan Lee: yes we'll do that today.
[03:51] Liam O'Connor: back to benchmarks: we also tried quantized int8 mode for a light profile, cost dropped ~38% but quality delta on longer generative tasks increased noise; Priya's team flagged hallucinations on two prompt classes. you may want to keep quant for classification and keep float16 for generative until we tune prompts.
[04:22] Priya Sharma: noted. what's the plan for tuning quantized weights — is that a model-reprofile or runtime param?
[04:28] Liam O'Connor: currently runtime param + we can recommend a quant profile which trades off some residual token accuracy; for deeper fixes we'd onboard a reprofile and run a quick eval job.
[04:36] Maya Gonzalez: for the ops handoff we proposed next week: final KV cache runs, SAML smoke test, and a short canary ramp in staging. once those are green we'll move to a formal handoff doc. ok?
[04:46] Jordan Lee: that fits our timeline, target to gate on 2027-05-26 for handoff readiness.
[04:52] Sara Kim: and we'll need the SOC2 scoping by 2027-05-24 to align audits.
[04:58] Liam O'Connor: to be specific about benchmarks i'll run 3 x 10k request sweeps with KV and without, capture p50/p95/p99 and raw latencies, and include node-level metrics and orchestration events.
[05:12] Priya Sharma: please include the exact SDK version and server build hash so we can match later.
[05:18] Liam O'Connor: will do, i'll paste them in the slack channel and attach the spreadsheet.
[05:25] Renee Park: i'll coordinate the handoff checklist and create the ops-runbook draft in confluence, link to the runbook in the next steps.
[05:33] Tom Alvarez: any notes about fallback policies? if a region has capacity issues we need a predictable fallback to smaller model variant.
[05:39] Maya Gonzalez: yes we can define a routing policy: primary regional endpoint -> fallback to smaller quantized model in same region -> fallback to hosted multi-tenant in another region. we'll include expected cost delta and latency delta in the runbook.
[05:56] Evan Mills: are there limits on concurrent connections? we expect bursts up to 600 rps in staging.
[06:02] Liam O'Connor: dedicated pool sizing is adjustable; for hosted pilot with our default pool the safe burst is about 250 rps without burst capacity. for 600 rps we'll either reserve dedicated capacity or configure a burst policy; i'll include recommended instance counts.
[06:20] Priya Sharma: for the evals we need token-level output so we can compute our custom metrics, can you provide a streaming hook?
[06:26] Liam O'Connor: streaming is available; we'll expose an SSE endpoint or websocket, whichever you prefer. streaming also reduces perceived latency on client side.
[06:34] Jordan Lee: small nit - the SDK's retry backoff behavior seemed aggressive, spawned duplicate requests in our retry tests; any config to tune?
[06:42] Liam O'Connor: yes you can tune client-side backoff. server dedupe for idempotent requests is in our backlog; current best practice is to set idempotency-key header.
[06:55] Maya Gonzalez: ok let's recap action items and owners. Liam, Jordan, Sara, Maya will be the main owners.

[07:02] -- Recap / explicit next steps --
[07:05] Maya Gonzalez: 1) Liam to share raw logs and 10k-run spreadsheet by 2027-05-20.
[07:14] Liam O'Connor: yep will do.
[07:16] Maya Gonzalez: 2) Brightline to complete VPC peering and share screenshots by 2027-05-21 (Jordan/Evan).
[07:23] Jordan Lee: on it.
[07:24] Maya Gonzalez: 3) Sara to send SOC2 scoping questions and contact by 2027-05-24.
[07:30] Sara Kim: will follow up.
[07:32] Maya Gonzalez: 4) Maya to send pilot pricing and new runbook draft by 2027-05-21.
[07:37] Maya Gonzalez: any final questions?
[07:40] Tom Alvarez: no just please include the expected cost delta for fallback to quantized model.
[07:44] Liam O'Connor: i'll include cost per token estimates for each model variant in the spreadsheet.
[07:48] Maya Gonzalez: great thanks everyone, we'll reconvene next Tuesday same time for a pre-handoff check.
[07:55] Jordan Lee: thanks all
[07:57] Priya Sharma: thanks
[08:00] (call ends)

Notes: minor stutters in transcription around 01:15 and 04:46; some proper nouns (like exact build hashes) omitted in transcript but will be shared in follow-up attachments.
